I picked this up because it was on sale and I wanted something to break the pace between the hours of adrenaline fueled shooters I've been playing (especially Doom Eternal and TItanfall 2) and Resident Evil 4 filled those shoes perfectly.

This is my first Resident Evil game so I can't comment on what they changed from previous titles, or how it influenced future games. 

Where should I start.
Initially I thought it'd be an extremely slow-paced, generic zombie shooter since I had no experience with any RE titles or any similar games in the genre. The closest I could think of is Alien: Isolation (which i liked.)
And I was partially right. The game WAS a slow zombie shooter for the first hours of the game, but then gradually expanded beyond that. The first act was the most 'Resident Evil' feeling out of them. You're trapped in this European village full of half-infected zombies, graveyards, and lots of fog. The second act however completely changed the setting into an evil castle scenario; complete with dungeons, haunted knight armor, and cultists with catapults. The third act just completely threw 'survival-horror' out the window and became a full on, balls-to-the-wall action movie. With explosions and ♥♥♥♥. It was insane. 
So yeah it wasn't really the experience I was looking forward to at first, but I gladly adapted.

The gameplay was a lot more fun than I thought. Sure, I couldn't use any crazy weapon combos like in Doom. But I could shoot a zombie in the leg, making them stumble and fall, then empty my clip by shooting their head multiple times to end it with a satisfying blast of blood and gore.
You couldn't do this often however; ammo is scarce and you need to pick your fights smartly, especially during the first act. Gradually though, you get more weapons as you spend your money on the funny merchant man. You can even upgrade your guns to get better stats.
The Striker shotgun feels orgasmic to shoot with and I want to make out with it.
Guns take a lot of space in your inventory however, and you'll need to reserve some space for other items. Speaking of the inventory system, I love it. Instead of having icons on boxes you have this grid system that was so easy to organize items in, and dare I say it, fun. I want more games to have this grid system.
Enemy variety was great. Guys with pitchforks. Guys with crossbows. Guys with hatchets. Guys with wolverine claws. Flying dudes. Big dudes. Doom 2 chaingunner. The Regenerators are my favorite enemy. They're cool.
The bosses were good too, nothing special. Shoot the obvious weakpoint till it dies, though sometimes it mixes it up a bit.
Being Resident Evil, there are bound to be some puzzles. Most of them consisted of just 'retrieve this item and put it in this very obvious engraving' but there are a few that stood out. The only puzzle I disliked was the one you had to solve as Ashley. It's just a swap-the-pieces puzzle and it even frustrated me for a bit. 

Maybe it's time to talk about the story and characters. You play as Leon, a very cool dude that is very much a cliche American action hero. Your mission is to save Ashley, the daughter's president, from an evil cult led by Saddler and his goons. Just another day at work. There are other characters like Luis, this spanish dude who smooth talks a lot and was kinda like your sidekick for a bit. Ada Wong, who was from RE2 and so I had no clue what her significance was. The Travelling Merchant was is the best character in the game. "Got some good things on sale stranger!" "Aah, I'll buy it at a high price." Incredible.
Ashley. Oh Ashley. Whiny little ♥♥♥♥♥. When they introduced the mechanic where you had to escort her, I audibly groaned. Thankfully, she was kidnapped for most of the game since I'm not fond of these companion characters in games (except for Elizabeth from Bioshock Infinite) so I hadn't need to worry. Though honestly, she wasn't so bad as a companion character. She'd duck your shots and stay out of combat most of the time. However she DOES have health and could die if taken enough damage which results in a game over. As for her shouting and screaming, let's just say that I had to restart at times because I kept shooting Ashley in the face. 
The main villain Saddler is a dude in a hoodie who would taunt you over the radio and is the leader of the cult. I didn't really take him seriously as he was such a comical unrealistic villain, but his banters with Leon were super entertaining to watch. Like sometimes he'd just laugh. He's funny. I don't really have a lot to say about the little dude guy in the castle. I mean his bodyguards are cool yeah

I don't really have issues with the game and I do think it's aged pretty well. EXCEPT for the QTE's.
Oh how I despise QTE's. And there are an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of them in this game. There are times I'd sit back thinking I'm watching a cutscene then bam. Press the button to not die. It's super bland and I had to repeat entire sections just cause I failed a single one. That didn't happen often though, so thank God.
Another issue isn't really from the game. It was the port. Sometimes the game would just alt-tab itself then alt-tab back continuosly. I don't know if I'm the only one with this issue but even then it only happens in this game.

I could go on and on and how there are minigames and treasures and you unlock like 5 expansions when you finish the game but I'm too tired. 
I don't know where to put this in the review so I'm gonna say it here. The game still looks great. The textures are sharp and high quality. Volumetric fog helps set the tone and thickens the atmosphere. Character animations and models are top notch and even though I had to sit through some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ QTE sections I got to see Leon doing cool ♥♥♥♥.

Anyways 8/10 cool cool game

I had never finished this game until now, and I don’t know why I waited so long. It’s a very good and fun experience. While it may not be as heavy on survival horror as the older titles (though still more than 5 and 6), that doesn’t take away from how great the game is. There’s definitely a stronger focus on combat, but it works perfectly for what this game set out to be; a more action oriented, over the top adventure.

Leon is awesome and delightfully cheesy, constantly throwing out one-liners and roundhouse kicking enemies. The villains are equally ridiculous, and most of the story leans into that same campy tone. But that’s part of what makes it so much fun.

The gunplay is classic Resident Evil style but without the fixed camera. You can aim freely, though you can’t move while aiming, and the game still uses tank style controls. It took a little time to adjust, but once I did, it felt great. The way enemies move and attack makes the system work surprisingly well.

The game is also a good length. It took me around 12 hours to finish on easy, which isn’t overly simple and mainly just provides more ammo while keeping enemies challenging. There’s also a great new game plus feature that carries over all your equipment. After beating the game you also unlock Mercenaries mode, a fast-paced horde mode, and two additional side stories.

Overall, this is an excellent game! It might not be exactly what every Resident Evil fan wants, but it never strays too far like 5 and 6 did. It’s a perfect balance of action and horror, and absolutely worth playing.

This is my favorite Resident Evil title.  After replaying it twice over the past week (once on normal, once on professional) I am happy to say that it still holds up.  It's a great game with some really cool stuff to unlock that was not present in the original versions of the game.  

Resident Evil 4 retains the heart of the series' survival horror while bringing a more linear, fast-paced, action-oriented design philosophy to the table.  This is a big set of changes from the first 3 games (and also Code Veronica X) so I fully understand why fans of them may not be into this.  But, the game wears those changes like a badge of honor and executes them really well.  You can tell the developers put a lot of passion into realizing their vision.  The weapons pack a punch which makes combat feel great, the characters and story are well written, and the environments are varied; it's a very well put together package.

I hold this game near and dear to my heart.  It's the installment I grew up on before my friend and I spent countless hours of our childhoods playing Resident Evil 5 together in local co-op.  Resident Evil 4 is a masterfully crafted classic.  If you decide to give it a shot, I've got a mission for you Agent Kennedy: have fun!

Let me start with the controls:
At first I thought I just had to get used to it, and even though I did get much better in handling the controls, they just simply suck. Not being able to strave left or right is so incredibly annoying. With Keyboard and mouse it is just unplayable, so I switched to controller. But turning around 90 degrees with a controller is just painfully slow.

Next the storyline:
What can I say? Resident Evil has never been famous for very good and deep storylines. It always contained a huge amount of cheesiness and awkward writing. But it always did have its serious and dark parts as well. In Resident Evil 4? It seems like they upped the cheesiness by 1000% Every line Leon says is just a stupid one liner. His overconfidence is highly annoying. 
Let's not talk about the main storyline anyway. We have to resque the president's daughter... by ourselves!?

Somewhat connected to the storyline is the setting of the game. The game takes play in this village somewhere in Europe. Already 5 minutes in the game you start murdering and blasting away the whole town. This game throws waves of enemies at you. I wonder how many people live in this village! Also the way the levels are designed makes it feel like the game takes place in the year 1900 or something. I understand a chance of scenery and theme is needed sometimes. But this felt so weird. And then you had these very random locations. What was that stupid huge robot level about? And the lava room with flamethrower dragons? And that knight statue becoming alive? Just very stupid! I know RE1 did not always make much sense with the house and its traps, but at least that was somewhat grounded in reality in some way. RE4 just has so many stupid things going on.

Some of the enemies were cool, but I did not like the main villains. Especially the small one with the pirate clothes. Why did they wear all these ridiculous clothes anyway? A parasite likes to wear clothes from the 1900? Why are there no televisions or anything like that in this town? The sewer level was more technologically advanced than the village. I am a bit worried 8 will also suffer from this.

The things I wrote above are just a small part of the annoyances in this game. There are many more.
Just don't create a game that throws waves of enemies at you while the action controls are very bad. I did like the part on the island a lot more. That part felt more like Resident Evil again. Though I could not fully enjoy it because of the horrible controls.

I was never a fan of Resident Evil. Never really played the games and whatever I did try, I always disliked. Resident Evil 0 was very micro-management heavy for me, not to even mention the puzzles that were too fiddly for me. I tried Resident Evil 4 twice before this as well. Both times I struggled with the inventory management and my own unnecessary stress levels since this is a game where you could technically softlock yourself. 

This time however I beat the game and I did it in only 3 days. It was just that fun. Turning the difficulty to Easy allowed me to enjoy the game more, still stress a bit, die a bunch while still seeing the story and environments. 

Other than the last chapter, this game's really bloody great. The village takes a familiar sight to many, a slightly run-down but still operational village and turns it unnerving while the castle takes a spooky concept of an old spooky castle and turns it into an unofficial sequel to Saw with the nonsensical contraptions and the absolute camp that the game embraces. Then there's the last chapter... yeah, it's terrible in every way. Other than a single interesting enemy, everything else is just a slog. Near endless amounts of enemies, most people using ranged in a game that has some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ movement controls in the history of gaming and such a lack of an interesting story that it might as well be a badly made fan project mod that just doesn't understand the game it's supposed to be in.

The controls are the infamous tank controls. Are they good? No. Are they usable? Yes. The game mostly (except the final chapter) understands what it's working with and so while it's clunky, the game also eases itself up to let you avoid most damage just by running forward. It's a bit mindless, sure, but somehow it instills a feeling of control over the environment and the enemies. And don't let people make you think otherwise. It's babying from the game due to the bad controls. This isn't some Machiavellian scheme to have some unique concept of the nature of horror or whatever else. 
Aiming's fine, but sluggish and weapons like the shotgun still require perfect on-the-dot aiming for any smaller target like snakes and environmental objects. 
It's clunky, but you can get used to it and the developers are aware of what they're working with. 

The story is generally understandable for a newcomer to the series. Characters are established and while Leon and Ashley themselves are complete vacuums of personality, all the villains have at least something to them. There's nothing elaborate and nothing very complicated to the story and it's alright that it doesn't. 

Graphically the game's dated. But also at the same time the HD version brings it to a limbo of being a bit modern while also being embarrassingly dated. Stretched rock textures that are 4 pixels by 4 pixels are commonplace and the environments feel pretty barren at times even at their tight sizes. But at the same time, Leon looks great and so does every other character. The film grain is obnoxious at times, but it definitely muddies the waters to make sure you don't focus on the bad textures. The lighting is pretty damn great, but there will be moments of seeing invisible light sources. 

But the biggest crux is Ashley, of course. The game's 50% an active escort mission. Luckily, she's stapled to you mostly and so she becomes more like a part of you, rather than some rogue agent ready to sabotage the mission. You'll have moments of her stepping into random bear traps and losing LITERALLY ALL OF HER HEALTH IN SECONDS but she also avoids some unnecessary headaches by essentially not even existing. Of course it's a lazy way of making a companion (similar to Ellie from The Last of Us or Elizabeth from Bioshock Infinite), but I'd rather have a ghost pretending to be a human than a sentient slice of bread masquerading as a person. What Ashley really lacks is being likeable. She is comically inept, she screams like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ banshee all the bloody time and just never becomes interesting in any way. Her privileged elf ear ass could've gotten stuck on the first bear trap for all I cared, but the game sadly really needed her along for the journey. 

If you're like me and hate puzzles, don't fret, all the puzzles are completely doable and almost braindead, which I appreciated. The difficulty of the game itself is also dynamic, which honestly made the game much more bearable with the sudden difficulty spikes at a couple of locations. 

So, if you were like me and never got into RE4, but already own it, give it a shot. I wouldn't recommend buying this unless it was at a sale with a small enough price that you wouldn't mind losing the money. This game's good and got me into the franchise, but to ignore the faults of the game would be foolish and to ignore the fact that it took me multiple tries to even get into it would also be a mistake.

[h1] Story [/h1]

After the events of Racoon City, Leon S. Kennedy was questioned by the U.S government, after giving his testimony on what occurred in Raccoon City. He, later on, was given training as an Agent of the U.S government to act like a Deployable Mercenary, to investigate, dispose of, and do any tasks in regards to taking care of B.O.Ws. 

The President's daughter has been captured, by Leons ex-comrade.  He captured her because he was tasked to by Saddler, the main villain, of the game, he has multiple henchmen which later on turn into monsters.  Salazar, the Village Cheif, and Krauser.  And Leon goes out of his way through every one of them. Then he, later on, goes to Saddler, the final boss. Requires the president's daughter, and rides into the sunset with a Jetski. 

[h1] The Gameplay [/h1]

This is a 2004 game, the controls are a bit clunky, and were designed for specific systems in mind, it is just a port, a good port. Frankly, in my opinion, as good as the 60 fps, I recommend capping at 30. Because certain enemies will flank you easily, due to the clunky controls. Granted that is just my bias.

[h1] Enviroment Design [/h1]

The game's atmosphere is spooky, dark & gritty. With plenty of greys & browns.  To contemplate the aspect. The overall environment is great, and it proves that. From the village areas to the caverns, castles, and the laboratory. Everything has its details, and contrast, in regards to something being "totally wrong" or something disturbing, took place.

[h1] Enemies & Enemy designs [/h1]

The enemies in this game are fairly great, you got your standard, human-like enemies which wield weaponry, and sometimes their skulls burst, with a weapon-wielding parasite. Then you got the mini-bosses, like that cool-looking scorpion thing, or that unholy abomination, you encounter with the elevators, deep underground. They are really challenging, but not in an obnoxious way. It's just your standard "find the pattern/weakness" Then you got your bosses like the EL Gigantes, or Saddler, or Salazer when he turns into a mutant ♥♥♥♥♥. Overall enemies are a solid 10. They are terrifying but in a cool way.

[h1] Some arbitrary things, I like [/h1]

I like the secret, treasures that you find throughout the game. For the old timy 3d designs of these things, I sure love the crowns, jewelry, etc.
I like the enemy designs, can't forget the kinky El Gigante.
Voice acting & Mocap, solid 10.
The plot, mmmmm....meh it is more of a blockbuster flick, not bad, but ain't my cup of tea.

Overall...my score.. is a SOLID 9/10.

one of the best resident evil games. but some people will find the controls and movement very off-putting if you havent played a traditional resident evil game before (e.g. the original trilogy, resident evil zero, code veronica, etc).

there are a few quick-time events which im not a huge fan of but these arent as common and annoying as in RE5. mostly you'll be dealing with slow-moving infected humanoid characters and a boss character at the end of each chapter. saves can be done at typewriters like in previous resident evil games but also at the end of chapters and a continue feature lets you restart if you die from the last checkpoint. 

all in all its a good game and will almost certainly be in line for the remake treatment after 2 & 3.

As much as I don't want to recommend RE4, I can't really fault a game for feeling dated when it was released back in 2005. Everything from moving, aiming your weapon, switch weapons, managing your inventory, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ QTEs... definitely does not hold up.

Then there's the difficulty scaling (game rank), so basically if you're doing too well on Easy or Normal, enemies will become more difficult until you start acting like a goof (missing shots, taking hits) or die. While I appreciate the thought of the game adjusting itself to keep pressure on the player, it does lead to an uneven experience at times. Such as unforgiving QTEs (how fast do you want me to mash the button?!), the most basic enemies become absurd bullet sponges, your inventory looking empty after boss fights (unless you came prepared with a rocket launcher every time). I actually preferred to play on Professional difficulty as everything was always cranked up to max and stayed that way (plus beating Separate Ways to unlock the knight armor costume for Ashley *chef kiss*).

As for the story, the plot and lines are like the cliche action/horror B movie schlock ("No thanks, Bro!" ...gets me every time). You either love it or hate it.

So if you want to relive your nostalgia or want to play a classic, by all means go ahead and be ready to take the time necessary to learn the tank controls. If not, just wait for the remake... in the next couple months... years...

Resident Evil 4 is one of the greatest horror games that exists for a reason. From the spectacular pacing to the steps it took to distinguish itself form its predecessors the game is a hallmark of the genre. In my time playing it found that it did not take long for me to get totally invested in playing, finishing a playthrough over the span of two days. While this gem of the series is not without it faults, it is still open of the pinnacle of said genre.

From the start capcom has strived to make sure you are playing a Resident Evil game, but made for the new age that the game came out on. (That being Playstation 2 and Gamecube respectively). While the game is a mixture of tank and over the shoulder gameplay it welcomes new and old players to the series. The various enemies, the weapons that you progressively upgrade or trade in for new ones and the characters themselves serve to draw the player in for a ride through its story. 

The only issue that new players may have is that this game was released in 2004. That is 16 years of progress for gaming that might turn some players away from this incredible game. Yes there are some dated mechanics that should you watch any speed run they abuse mercilessly, but its still a great ride from start to finish

Would I Recommend? 100%

The problem with this game is that it basically sheds the survival/horror/puzzle background of the earlier RE games, but as an actioner this game fails to offer compelling gameplay. In fact, RE4 is boring af. Like even by 2005 standards, this would have been boring. I have literally spent the last hour in-game just fighting normal mobs, one or two at a time, and the game still hasn't finished spawning them. This game is in worse need of a remake than I remembered. The awful tank controls need to go because strafing actually does exist, Leon needs to be able to at least walk while aiming (or knifing), the combat/gameplay needs a tune up, and the quick-time mechanics need to be cleaned up (e.g., the terrible "Kick" quick-time button that pops up randomly only ~50% of the time when you stun an enemy, so the other 50% when you run up to his melee range but DON'T get the quick-time prompt, then he slashes you in the face because Leon is so slow to pull out the knife or do anything else). And I haven't even gotten to the part of the game with the helpless Ashley AI yet. There are a lot of frustrations here that could be improved for a better user experience in 2021.

UPDATE: Now deeper into the game (final chapter), its incredible flaws are even more obvious. I guess this is why the community relies on the Ditman glitch to a.) increase Leon's movement & action speed to something more tolerable, but more importantly b.) bypass large sections of the game (e.g., some of the lame mob encounters). It's ironic to think this glitch hinges on going into the inventory to equip/change weapons, which shouldn't even be a thing. You should be able to cycle through weapons on the fly. It's immersion breaking to constantly be pausing the action mid-fight to go into the inventory (regardless of whether I'm just switching weapons or specifically going into inventory to reactivate the glitch following one of this game's million cut scenes).

Then you've got the quick time events. Is this the lamest mechanic in the history of video gaming? The Krauser fight for instance, where you're on a strict time limit and your ability to shoot the boss is interrupted every two seconds by quick time events. Or god forbid you ever try to take a drink during a cut scene, because you're dead. But this game is so old it doesn't have native controller support, so the game will give you 0.5 seconds to spam some random key on the keyboard, and I will have to die and then go into the keybinds to figure out what that key's bound to. Then I reload, redo the quick time scene... but this time it randomly changes to a different key. So I die again. Repeat. Or there was one sequence where I had 0.5 seconds to spam Left Click to dodge Left. Well, in that 0.5 second window when I needed to dodge Left, do you really think I remembered that Left Click is actually bound to *RIGHT* Trigger? Die. Repeat.

One time I had to redo an entire 30-minute sequence due to failing the [i]second[/i] of [i]multiple[/i] quick time events following the mine cart sequence. When I reloaded, I was all the way back two rooms before the start of the mine carts. As if I weren't angry enough at this game already, then it forces me to replay sections due to lame mechanics where I'm not even in control of my character. But at least the game gives you rocket launchers to one-hit KO all of the bosses and mini-bosses, right? It's as if the devs are acknowledging their own poor game design by giving you a way to bypass around the encounters. Well you better take it, because in this game it's either cheese or be cheesed. Thanks devs. 10/10. Would play again on Professional Mode just for fun.

I'm glad I got around to playing this game, and I can see why it's a fan favorite. 

First off, the pacing is excellent. There are many tense moments, but you never feel like you're pushed over the edge. Right when things reach a peak in intensity, they slow down shortly after and provide some pleasant breathing room. These moments are usually accompanied by a cut scene, or maybe a merchant, and a save point. The save points and checkpoints are placed perfectly, making it never feel too tedious if you die and have to repeat a small chunk.

Now, for the game play. Some people complain about the controls, but I don't know what they're talking about. This game has fine controls, and they only get easier as you keep playing. The action is fun and satisfying. It never gets old roundhouse kicking a ganado in the face or hearing those heads pop with a good head shot. One thing that may be annoying at first is having to open your inventory screen every time you want to switch weapons, but you get use to it quickly. At least the inventory screen pauses the action, so there's no rush.

Finally, a little about the story and characters. It's fun. The characters are entertaining. There is rarely a dull moment. The villains are menacing and mysterious, and the allies.. Well, you've heard probably the jokes about Ashley, but she's a better character than you'd initially believe. That's all I'll say without spoiling anything.

Overall, I've been enjoying my time with RE4, and I recommend it not only to Resident Evil fans, but to anyone who hasn't played this all around classic of a game.

The game is good. A lot of people say that this game changed resident evil, but honestly? The only difference between this game and other resident evil games is that it is slightly more action oriented. There are more enemies and the gunplay is faster paced than the other games that came before. Everything else is more or less the same. The game still has puzzles, the game still has crazy twisted boss fights, and the game still has an inventory system that has to be managed. Granted, a lot of those mechanics are slightly dumbed down (inventory management is much easier due to keys and treasures being put in a separate inventory).

Another thing, the game is not scary. Okay, I didn't get scared. I wouldn't even really consider this to be a horror game outright, just an action adventure game that has a slightly spooky tone. Some encounters are also slightly more tense than others.

The worst part of this game is the damn quick time events. This game really likes to put them in the middle of cutscenes (ya know, the time where us gamers take a drink and rest), and these quick time events often interrupt normal gameplay and ruin certain bosses. Also, if you play the game at 60 FPS be prepared for the quick time events to be extremely off in the timing. You gotta spam x faster than the speed of light to get past the minecart part. 

Either way, the game is good. Get it, play it, have fun.

For reference, I played RE 1 and 2 on PS1 back in the days, Re 1,2 and 3 remakes and RE 7. This this by far the worst entry in the series for me.

1 - It's not a resident evil by any mean. The characters come from the franchise obviously but none of the Resident Evil game mechanics are there. I knew that it was more action focused but it goes beyond that. It plays like a 3rd person shooter with a bit of ammo management (You got plenty enough but you shouldn't go too crazy either). It should have been a spin off of the franchise. Not the 4th iteration.

2 - It fails completely as a 3rd person shooter. Maybe I'm a bit harsh cause it's a very old game and IIRC, the 3rd person shooter genre was fairly new back in the day, but everything feels cheap:
	- The control are horrendous - takes half an hour to do a quarter turn and you don't 	have any lateral movement. "Nop I can't escape. have to do my very long quarter 	turn first...oops I got hit"
	- the aiming system is the worst I've ever seen in that kind of game - you aim 			with the laser (that's not how you use a laser on a gun) and for some reason your 		character have the Parkinson disease. I don't mean the aim should remain still but 		it way too excessive to the point of being ridiculous.

3 - I know Resident Evil are supposed to be cheesy, but this one somehow takes the wrong direction. Previous RE were B horror movies. This one is a B action movie. There are amazing environments, a fittingly creepy atmosphere for its setting, very satisfying gun-play and variety of weapons, a simple but satisfying upgrade system, and a really fun tone throughout. It's not scary in the slightest, no real jumpscares or freak out moments. It's like a cheesy fun action movie. Don't go in expecting to be scared. It also has a lot of content. The main campaign is really long, and has a lot of stuff for you to see.

Then there are the bonus modes on top of that, unlocked by beating the main story once. Completing these modes unlocks extra stuff for a new playthrough of the main campaign. Mercenaries doesn't take too long to 5 star everything, even with all the characters, but it is a fun mode if you just want to shoot as many enemies as possible. Then there are two extra smaller but still very quality campaigns that you get to, one of them is canon and explains some of the stuff that a Ada was doing in between her off screen time and what her goals were. It feels like if these campaigns/modes were released in a modern game they would be released as a dlc or preorder bonus for the game. These would be well worth buying as dlc though. I only hope that they don't touch the gameplay or modes too much when Capcom inevitably tries to remake this game. 

My only complaints are that the game will chug at certain points in the game, I believe you can fix this but it is pretty inexcusable for an hd port of this game to not fix that by default. Another is that the options in the menu for graphics and audio feel like a joke, just not enough there. I should add that the game only crashed once on me, not a good thing to happen, but it only happened once throughout an entire playthrough, that's not bad at all when you consider how long that campaign is.

Overall I think the game is a lot of fun, even after all this time. It feels like a timeless game that nailed everything right, and is an outstanding example of its own genre, and series for that matter. Don't be deterred if you haven't played any of the other Resident Evil games, it's pretty self contained, there are like 2 characters from this game that appear in other games that aren't Leon, and you can get a lot of the info on them in this game, especially if you play Ada's campaign. By all means go play the other Resident Evil games, they're great and you don't need me to telll you that. Except maybe 6 lol. But don't feel the need to go in order, cause this game is a fan/series favorite for a reason. Play the ones that look good to you, but be sure to place this in there somewhere.

Resident Evil 4 is not "the greatest game of all time." It's not even the greatest Resident Evil game of all time. Survival horror elements are all but shed for the first time in the series, the plot is paper-thin, and, aside from the inclusion of a couple legacy characters (Leon and Ada), it has very little to do with the rest of the games as far as narrative is concerned. All that said, I feel the same way I felt about 2020's Resident Evil 3 Remake; this game is rad! The boss fights are super fun, it doesn't veer as far from the series' roots as later sequels, and I really do love a lot of the characters in this game. Ramon Salazar is probably my favorite Resident Evil villain (in contention with Nemesis and Jack Baker), Leon comfortably slots into the "early 2000s action hero" archetype, and Ashley is not nearly as annoying as people claim she is. Overall, it doesn't quite live up to the hype, but there's still plenty to love here and I don't regret a single second I spent with the game.

Resident Evil 4: Ultimate HD Edition Review

The defining point in Resident Evil made an HD comeback!

Some key points that this game offers:

1.	HD Visuals
2.	60 Frames Per Second
3.	Complete Visual Overhaul
4.	Fully optimized for Widescreen

Ultimate HD Edition:

It came at a great time, you can never get enough Resident Evil, that much is pretty obvious. They play great, the story is fantastic and Zombies man! These games defined the Survival Horror genre and without them, we wouldn’t have what we have today.

Albeit RE4 being more Action Horror, it still offers enough survival mechanics to keep the essence of what RE is about. These games all pretty much released way back then and they have not aged well with all the technological breakthroughs we’ve had over the years. 

However, with some tweaking and overhauling they managed to give RE4 an HD makeover bringing it back so that we can re-experience this amazing game. A lot of work has been done to bring this game up to more current standards.
We have HD visuals and textures running up to 60 frames per second, which truly is bliss. Texts have been sharpened and textures on characters, in game objects, and backgrounds were improved to offer a more visually appealing appearance. The game has also been fully optimized for widescreen and undergone a complete visual overhaul enhancing every visual aspect of the game.

On PC there are some additional extras as well. Keyboard and mouse support with customizable key bindings and mouse sensitivity and acceleration options. There is also a variety of subtitle support now; English, French, Italian, German, and Spanish.

Then we also get access to the bonus content Separate Ways.

MGR Gaming’s Conclusions:

Chances are you don’t even need my opinion to go and replay this masterpiece. If you enjoyed it the first time around then you are going to have a blast reliving those experiences. Everything just looks better and tweaked to give us a more acceptable visual standard when compared to other games currently being released.

They did an amazing job here. Everything looks great, sure the game is still old; it shows you that in the script which might come off as ‘cheesy’ this time around. The setting and game mechanics further proves that but this is not a remake it’s a makeover of a classic and that is exactly what we have here.


They gave the game a great makeover and for those of us who played it when it was released originally way back then, it offers a variety of not again and other nostalgia memories. Players new to the series have just as much to gain and enjoy from this game and I urge you to give it a shot. 

The game that changed it all is back and it never looked better! Be sure to give it your time, you will not regret it!

I've played this game 40 times in my entire life. First on ps2 and then on ps3, now on a computer.  This is the best game of its kind and I love it.  But such a legendary game has its own nuances.

Advantages:

 + Addictive gameplay.
 + Lots of content and decent replayability.
 + The best bosses in the series.  Both in design and in the battle process.
 + Nice visual design.
 + The right balance between action and suspense inherent in past games in the series.
 + Interesting plot.  Since RE2, the protagonist has matured a lot, which is an interesting game of contrasts.  In many ways, this is a great merit of the voice actor Paul Mercier.

Disadvantages:

 - There are few puzzles and they are too easy.  Not that they were complicated in the previous parts, but in the four they were too simplified.

 - The final third of the game is prolonged, and some of its episodes (beginning of Chapter 5-1, Chapter 5-4) should have been cut out.

 - Despite the fact that the publication is positioned as an HD version, it is impossible to look at the resolution of textures in the castle without tears, although good work has been done in other places.  And if in the main game, the cutscenes look normal, then in the campaign for the second character they were transferred without changes from the very first port.

 - Many of the game's plot elements are sorely lacking in backstory and additional explanations.  For many questions, the game simply does not provide any answers.

 ✔ Despite all its flaws and controversial points, RE4 is still a great game to return to every time.  Let's hope that the upcoming remake will correct the flaws of the original, and make the pluses more visible.

This is the first horror game I've ever played and, despite my initial hesitation, it ended up completely engrossing me. The controls may have aged poorly in places, but the systems in place are excellent and force you to carefully manage all of your resources, creating some very tense heart-pounding situations. Unlike what I've heard about previous entries in the series, this game is very combat-focused, and that scared me away at first. But it's so well done and there's so much variety in the combat situations that I ended up not caring about the lack of puzzles. The pacing in this game is masterful. It never holds your hand, but it never leaves you up the creek without a paddle, and this makes gameplay that could have easily felt repetitive into a captivating experience that will make you want to see things out to the very end. Like any game, it has its shortcomings: the controls that I alluded to before, some of the vehicle segments, quick-time events that kill you instantly for not reacting fast enough, and one particularly dumb boss fight. But none of that takes away from the well-crafted and addicting core experience. If you're not usually into horror or shooters like me, I cannot stress enough that you need to give this game a shot. It may take some time to get used to how to play, as it did for me, but after pushing my way through and finishing, I can confidently say that RE4 deserves its status as a masterpiece.

[h1]Intro[/h1]
[h3](Spoiler-Free Review)[/h3]
[b]Resident Evil 4[/b] is a third-person survival horror set in early 2000s rural Spain. Players impersonate Leon S. Kennedy, a special agent tasked with recovering the US President's daughter, Ashley, who was kidnapped by a mysterious cult called Los Illuminados. Very soon his investigation becomes the fabric of nightmares, as Leon will find himself facing hordes of hostile villagers, mutated abominations and cult leaders on his arduous path to save Ashley.

🟩 [b]The Good Side[/b]
[list]

[*][b]A hero's odyssey[/b]
Leon's journey will span across rural villages, medieval castles and even secret military bases across the Spanish countryside. Each area has several unique enemies to match and as well diverse dangers such as hidden traps - the solid variety in terms of enemies, bosses and situations allows RE4 to stay fresh until the end. Balance-wise, the game shines especially during the first half, when Leon's weapons and equipment are still relatively weak and enemies dangerous - a few hits are all it takes to kill the protagonist, in fact.

[*][b]More than meets the eye[/b]
It wouldn't be a true Resident Evil without each area being filled with secrets and hidden items for the more attentive players to discover. Exploration plays a crucial role, as finding most treasures and secondary areas will drastically improve monetary gains by selling valuables, consequently allowing more upgrades. Other than that, plenty of ammunition and useful consumables are also scattered everywhere. Usually the most difficult segments or boss fights have some hidden nuance or mechanic to make them easier, however not always obvious to find at first.

[*][b]It's not over yet![/b]
Finishing the main story unlocks a bounty of additional modes and extras, adding more content. "The Assignment" and "Separate Ways" are two spin-off short campaigns where players impersonate another important character of RE4's story, while "The Mercenaries" is a score-attack mode, where one can play in iconic story locations with a roster of different characters from the RE franchise, such as Wesker for instance. Each of these extra characters has unique abilities, weapons to match and there even is a unique map with special enemies in this mode only.
[/list]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2373628574

🟥 [b]The Bad Side[/b]
[list]

[*][b]Quick-time stupidity[/b]
Quick time events are a stupid mechanic to begin with in any game, however in RE4 they are further aggravated by the clunky keyboard + mouse controls. Half-a-second long prompts such as "O+P" or "X+C" will be common in several boss fights and cutscenes - failing one of these usually means instant death. Having to re-do an entire section or boss fight because of this is very frustrating.

[*][b]Harder! I said harder![/b]
RE4 shares, with some other survival horrors, the pointless decision of barring the hardest difficulty (Professional) behind finishing the game to unlock it. Since the replay value is negligible, not many players will feel inclined to replay the exact same adventure again. This mechanic is a remnant of an outdated game design mentality, which penalizes returning players that may have already cleared the game many times over - and could use the hardest setting from the start.

[*][b]Too strong for your own good[/b]
If the balance for roughly the first half of RE4 is quite good and challenging at times, it becomes increasingly broken as the story advances after that. Leon will acquire a formidable arsenal of upgraded weapons (unless he wasted money and missed most valuables, that is) that will obliterate any foe and boss with relatively small effort. The amount of ammunition, consumables and utilities like grenades found in the environment also becomes too great.
[/list]

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]
🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Combat, Character Management and Puzzles.

[b]Exploration[/b]
Is performed on foot, Leon can either walk or run at no penalty, and climb low ledges or perform other contextual action depending on the location (such as jumping off a window). While exploring, breakable containers in the shape of wooden barrels, crates and closed drawers, nightstands or shelves will be present in each area - finding as many as possible is essential to keep one's stocks of ammo, healing and utility items on decent levels. Secret items and valuables are also hidden in many places, such as on ceilings, inside bird nests that seem like a decoration, and more.

A map of each location is available from the start, however treasures will be visible on it only by purchasing a Treasure Map from the mysterious merchant. Generally each area's layout is linear, however there is a good number of secondary paths that often house extra goods, so checking out every nook and cranny is recommended.

[b]Combat[/b]
Plays out in third person, using an array of firearms such as pistols, shotguns and even rocket launchers. Most enemies have hit-contextual reactions, for example shooting one in a leg will make it fall, while a headshot will cause a stun and major damage. These stun-states can often be followed up by a melee special attack which doesn't consume ammo and delivers good damage. Melee is also a normal option via the knife, however should only be used as last resort, as it's unwieldy and weak.

Utilities such as grenades are powerful, but fairly rare and one-time use only. While in combat it's possible to stop time to open the inventory and use healing items at any time, or select another weapon. Bosses have usually various "stages" where they use diverse attacks and expose weakpoints at times, knowing where to shoot and when to fall back is essential.

[b]Character Management[/b]
Is performed by organizing the Briefcase, in which players can freely move and rotate all items to best fit them in the available space. Most of the time, one won't be able to carry every single item found, so something has to stay behind. The mysterious merchant is also available from a certain point, standing at fixed locations ready to trade valuables for money, sell new weapons, accessories and upgrade existing ones. Ammo however is not sold and is a crucial resource left to only players to find.

[b]Puzzles[/b]
Are often fairly simple logic-based enigmas, such as pressing buttons in a specified order or reconstruct an image from moving tiles. Certain valuables can also be "upgraded" with specific items by Combining them, so they will sell for more.

[b] Overview [/b] 
It’s the early year lull for game releases and this year I’ve found myself passing the time by diving headfirst into the Resident Evil franchise. Though I’ve played a good number of the RE titles over the years, I’d never played through 5 until a friend and I decided to co-op it just after New Year’s. To say the least, I enjoyed it more than I expected. It sent me down the rabbit hole and soon I found myself diving into a replay of 4 over a decade after I’d originally played it and I’m currently playing through Revelations for the first time. I’ve been having a blast so I decided to add one of my favorite series to my list of reviews.

[b] The Rook’s All Grown up [/b]
Resident Evil 4 has us returning to the role of Leon Scott Kennedy who is now a federal agent in a counterterrorism organization instead of a fresh-faced and bushy-tailed rookie in the Raccoon City police force. Thanks to this impressive new position, when the president’s daughter is kidnapped and it’s assumed to be an inside job, it’s Agent Kennedy that’s tasked with recovering her all on his lonesome. The mission starts out with him exploring a village packed full of particularly aggressive residents and leads through a dreary countryside, dark subterranean passages, and even a castle that would make Bowser jealous. Throw in a mysterious merchant who seems to always be wherever you need him to be and a variety of weapons to get your hands on and there’s a good amount of content to keep you occupied throughout the length of your rescue attempt.

[b] A Break from Tradition [/b] 
The classic Resident Evils (1-3) all felt similar from a gameplay standpoint. They were clear survival horror titles where it was just as often wise to navigate around and outmaneuver enemies than it was to murder them. There were certainly epic boss fights and it wasn’t rare to eliminate enemies that were in a particularly inconvenient position, but the action came secondary to the oppressive atmosphere.

Resident Evil 4 was the first to stray from this path. The tank controls were touched up and modified, free aiming became possible, and an over-the-shoulder camera was adopted that replaced the cinematic angles that the previous titles were known for. Survival horror plays second fiddle to the action of 4, though it wasn’t almost entirely forced out like the titles that would follow. It’s an exciting change, but one that also feels like something has been lost.

[b] Leon, Help! Help Me, Leon! [/b] 
The atmosphere of Resident Evil 4 is a step down from those that came before it. Though the countryside is designed in a way that you truly feel like you’re in a hostile and foreign land, many of the environments have clearly been made to prop up the combat system. This means that most maps are much larger than they’d need to be in a tighter horror experience; with far more territory to explore, each individual area loses some of what makes it stand out as unique. As a matter of fact, some areas don’t stand out from those around them at all, a far cry from the Spencer Mansion which many of us vividly remember every room of.

Without question, the most underwhelming element of the experience is Ashley Graham, the president’s daughter. The writing of her character isn’t noticeably worse when compared to the rest of the cast that surrounds her, though she brings with her Capcom’s first attempt at a heroic duo in the series and it’s ugly. When she’s around, you’ll have to watch out for her as she’ll be attacked by your foes as readily as they’ll come after you and she’s nowhere near as talented at avoiding them. If they don’t maul her to death and instead opt to throw her over their shoulder and take off with her, you’ll be picked them off instead of enemies that are more of a threat to you. If she goes down or is carried out of the scene, it’s a game over. Fortunately, it’s more annoying than difficult to keep her out of harm’s way and the auto-saves are placed in ideal locations throughout the adventure.

[b] Verdict [/b] 
Resident Evil 4 breaks away from the survival horror mold of the previous titles in the series and creates its own identity as something of a hybrid of the old and the new. Pulling off a second playthrough after over a decade away has proven to me that it’s entirely worthy of its classic status as it still remains an excellent experience that hooked me from start to finish in a way that most modern releases are unable to. It holds up well after all of these years, particularly with the upgrades that came with the Steam version, though you won’t want to jump into it expecting a fully modernized shooter or mind-blowing graphics. If you’re considering revisiting it for nostalgia’s sake, I find it unlikely that you’ll be disappointed. If you’ve never played it before, what are you waiting for?

Spoiler-Free review
[u] TLDR: Recommended if you enjoy action, but not if you are looking for a similar experience to RE0 - RE3. [/u]

[b] Gameplay [/b]

Quite comparable to modern Third-Person shooters, with the exception of strafing not being a thing, and aiming with your gun freezes you and your camera in place. You can jump through windows, jump from heights (And gain no fall damage) Mouse and Keyboard is recommended.

[b] Story [/b]

It's been years after the events of Resident Evil 2 and 3, and Leon Kennedy has been sent to a village where they suspect the president's daughter has been taken to. It is your job to rescue her. However, that is easier said than done...

[b] Compared to previous installments [/b]

RE4 has little in common with RE0 - RE3, remakes or originals. Compared to the originals, RE4 lacks the puzzle solving aspects, horror elements, and the camera works differently due to being the first third person game in the series. Storywise, the game is not focused about Umbrella anymore. If you enjoyed RE0 - RE3 for its atmosphere and puzzles, sorry, you won't find that here.

[b] Graphics [/b]

This game was first released on the GameCube, and it shows, textures are very low resolution, and the FOV is way too low at default, widescreen support is poor as well. However these three problems can be fixed by modding. But what can't be fixed? Models are of higher fidelity compared to other games in 2005, but definitely lacks compared to 2021's standards, however, many areas are very small and lack the aliveness found in newer games. On the positive side, the game runs perfectly on any system you throw at it, and runs at many resolutions, 1080p, 4k being included. The game can be locked to either 30 or 60 fps.

[b] Conclusion [/b]

Resident Evil 4 is a great game if you look past it being more than 16 years old, its gameplay and graphics are rough thanks to that. But it's story is something that can still be appreciated today. However, for people (like me) who love RE0 - RE3, it's not the same. I recommend getting used to the new gameplay, as the franchise sticks to it till RE7. 

I rate this game an 7.5, it's fun, just not as fun as the previous entries.

Resident Evil 4 is an action adventure, "horror" title from Capcom that is one of the most recognizable games of the gamecube era. The reason the horror was in quotations was because this really isn't a horror game. There are a moderate amount of tense moments, and the opening to RE4 tricks you into thinking this is a horror game. In reality this is a straight up action game, and that plays to its favor. Keeping the combat tight while introducing third person camera into the RE Franchise. Add a large enemy variety, and generally more enemies, and you've got a refreshing take on RE. When it comes to story RE4 isn't winning any awards with cheesy lines, weak dramatic tension, and underdeveloped characters. But on the other hand there are tons  of fan service moments, references, and genuinely funny gags. It feels like they went all out with pros and cons of FULL display. That factor really plays into the charm of RE4. In terms of content the story mode is lengthy, and upon completion there is an alternate story mode, and a downright fantastic arcade mode. Overall would I recommend RE4? Hell yes! To anyone interested in the RE franchise, this is the title to play. 8/10 Great game

[h3]On Ports[/h3]
Some call this one a bad port. Ha! Those lucky people who did not catch it, you have no idea how terrible the PC port of RE4 was back then. I had to use a glitchy third-party crack just to be able to play with a mouse (having dedicated controller support on PC wasn't common), which behaved ghastly. It still does to an extent, yet to me, the controls in this port feel perfect in comparison. I don't know how, but even then I managed to have fun, despite all the tripe, not to mention now. When talking about ports, mediocre beats terrible hands-down.

But hey, you should've seen me playing MGS 2 - there were [b]nine[/b] keys for each analog stick... I'll let your imagination do the rest. This port here is good enough, and while it isn't the Gamecube version by far (the lighting is kinda flat and all that), it does the job without major glitches. Well, if you don't count occasional QTE and high enemy damage oddities linked to the game being run at non-native 60 fps. They aren't that bad, except for that QTE at the end of the mine kart ride in Chapter 4, which is barely doable. Even so, the game isn't hard, so I did let it have its vengeance gleefully.

[h3]Story & Setting[/h3]
It's a fair price for the many moments of amusement and laughter that it bestowed upon me in exchange. RE4 has the charm of The Evil Dead and the characters of early Kojima's games. The game certainly pulls off the disgusting side of body horror - all the pestilence, parasites, and maggots affected me greatly. But for the most part, what transpires is simply hilarious, not scary. One of the main villains is literally a midget Hitler dressed like Napoleon... who at one point sends a giant stone robot midget after you! The iconic merchant alone always made me laugh. Anyone remembers that Mega64 skit with him? Seriously, look it up even if you've seen it already.

But for a zany anime that it is, the game sure builds its world with care. What a miserable place! They've really nailed that Ass European countryside atmosphere and the dichotomy between Baroque and mud. The castles' interiors are excessively lush, but everything else is cold water, cold dumplings, dogs and people bark together desperately. A bleak board hell that traps and tortures the souls of its victims who occasionally set each other's barns on fire for reasons most petty. But mainly just slowly drink themselves to death, dissolving into nothingness. If any kind of virus or a bomb would put an end to such existence, it should be considered a mercy kill.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
Here comes our sassy boy Leon! To gun down these people and their dogs, their insect gods, and even their funny midget king. The shooting feels proper thanks to the meaty hit sounds and frequent headsplosions. The game emphasizes tricky crowd control in gimmicky multi-storied arenas where every enemy is capable of insane damage output. It encourages careful positioning and deliberate maneuvering, which you must perform while aiming at different body parts for desired effects. Thereby, the game's combat features plenty of tactical depth, especially since Leon often has to deal with many enemies at once in confined spaces, which is the whole shtick. Or rather half of it.

The other half is hunting for them shiny treasures and see them drop from enemies, which is so delightfully gamey - it's one of those silly conventions that I always love to see in any game, no matter how realistic it strives to seem. It's just endlessly satisfying! And up until the very end, you don't get too much dough since weapon upgrades, inventory expansions, grenades, healing items, and all that goodness remain a perfect money sink that keeps injecting streams of dopamine right into your brain. And you know what? This kind of chemical reaction never gets old.

[h3]Ashley[/h3]
Ashley didn't cause me any trouble at all. I think that the devs did their best to make escorting her as painless as possible. This argument is supported by the fact that she can usually be thrown into a dumpster and forgotten about until it's safe to traverse. She also gets plot-kidnapped all the time. Either way, she's doing her best to keep close, her pathfinding is okay, and she even ducks while you aim! Clever girl. I didn't get the complaints when I first played the game, and I still think that they're exaggerated. Even if she manages to get kidnapped, the locations are tiny and there's an autosave at the start of each one of them. This isn't Silent Hill 4 is what I'm saying.

[h3]FOV[/h3]
Archaic designs like the suffocating FOV, tank controls, or the necessity to open your inventory to pick a gun instead of switching them on the fly didn't bother me, I even found most of them heartwarming instead. Despite my lenient attitude, these can be deal-breakers to some, but I believe that the game is worthwhile notwithstanding. Besides, Capcom has improved on countless little things by the time RE2 Remake came out, so there's no good reason to berate them for not performing the grand experiment that was RE4 perfectly right away.

You can actually do something about the FOV. Personally, I found the default value unpleasantly nauseating, which didn't happen to me before. I guess I'm getting old. Anyway, there's a useful little app called Flawless Widescreen that helped me out again, previously I used it for the non-remastered version of Bioshock 2. Did it give me an unfair advantage? Maybe, but I didn't go overboard with the value, it somewhat compensates for the fps glitches, plus I think the game not only plays but also looks better this way.

[h3]"Good. Bad. I'm the guy with the gun."[/h3]
So, um, does RE4 hold up? Not particularly well. Does it care that it doesn't? Nah, it spits on your shoe and laughs. And you either start laughing with it or scram. Both are valid choices, I don't blame anyone who can't get along with this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But personally, I appreciate the game for what it is. Yep, it's a mediocre port and a wacky, awkward take on the genre that doesn't always deliver a particularly deep horror experience, but it makes up for that with unabashed hilarity and tactical combat.

P.S. A fellow in the comments told me that the genre is `Panic Horror`, and yeah, I'm down with the term (coined by Shinji himself?). This is exactly what it is.

[h1] A New Era for Resident Evil [/h1]
After four mainline Resident Evil games, including Code Veronica, the RE formula was beginning to get stale. Due to this, Capcom decided to take the series in a completely different direction. Gone are the fixed camera angles, constant backtracking, and complicated puzzles. Now, combat has a larger focus, quick-time events are plentiful, and the story is more bizarre. While this was a massive departure from the previous entries, Resident Evil 4 manages to be one of the most complete and best games in the series. Whether it's the story, gunplay, or atmosphere, RE4 perfects nearly everything it attempts. Now, while there are some things that I dislike, such as the quick-time events, on the whole, RE4 is an extremely solid game. However, like many Capcom games, this is not a very good port. The game, while it has a 60FPS option, still runs many animations at 30FPS. Additionally, mouse acceleration is always on, the "HD Textures" aren't very good, and some audio lines fail to play. However, even though this is a pretty poor port, there are many community-made mods that fix these issues. Still, though, this is a very disappointing port. Overall, even though Resident Evil 4 took the series in a different direction, it still manages to be an excellent game. While the port isn't great and there are some annoying mechanics, everyone should still give Resident Evil 4 a try.

This port might not be as bad as the original 2007 RE4 PC port but it's still kinda trash:
* Badly optimized, a PC that can run RE5 and 6 smoothly might not be able to run this one well.
* If your monitor doesn't support 60hz the game won't even work.
* 60 fps mode accelerates many animations and occurences to 2x speed, and makes QTEs harder, and weird to look at.
* Stretched UI on 16:9
* Awful Motion Blur effect on by default
* Horrible FOV that will easily make you sick
* After some cutscenes, some kind of motion blur activates (even if you have it off in the options) and the only way to fix it is to restart the game.

Some of these issues, like the UI and the FOV, can be fixed with fan-made mods, but there are way too many problems overall that you'll just have to deal with. This is incredibly dissapointing considering how good other RE games are on PC, and makes this version not really that "Ultimate HD" compared to the Gamecube/Wii versions.

I only recommend getting it on a sale, and if you are willing to spend time to get the fan-made fixes. Because deep down the game is still great.

In the original games I find myself shooting once and running past them and in 5 and 6 I end up playing a worse version of Max Payne. In 4 I'm playing something I can't really get anywhere else, 

The combat feels incredibly smooth despite being stationary while aiming. It adds a level of intensity and commitment to shooting someone without making me feel like I'm rolling dice to see if I get to kill it in 3 shots or 15 shots like in RE2's Remake. There's a lot of satisfying weight to the melee actions that give you i-frames in order to make some space in a crowd. You constantly find yourself in new encounters with enemies that feel different from the last which is great, without that variety this game wouldn't really go far past the first few areas.

Boss fights are great. There's a few that I would call my favorite in the franchise and they really are satisfying. They all feature great set pieces and have the variety needed to keep each encounter unique. Some are better than others,  but you'll walk away from them all feeling accomplished

The inventory management leads to some satisfaction in sorting items around to tightly fit a rocket launcher you just picked up, and the upgrades lead to a sigh of relief. Rebind your sorting controls if you can, they can be a little awkward, but they're nothing worth bringing the game down over. 

You end up getting a lot of ammo from encounters, but there's still a need for precision and resource management. You don't get an infinite amount of ammunition to plow through enemies, but you're not gonna have to knife every enemy to try and conserve bullets. Melee actions after stunning an enemy is where the combat goes from engaging to enthralling.

The story is about what you'd expect from Resident Evil, it's nothing profound, but it's not bad either. It's actually quite good and fun. The characters are quiet like-able and there's game play sections that make them feel more personal than other entries. The game overall has really good pacing and never leaves me desiring something more.

The puzzle solving in this game is really fun. It's a nice way to break up the pace of the action encounters without resulting in mediocre gameplay. That's really all I have to say about it as they pretty much speak for themselves.

Lastly, this game doesn't ditch horror entirely. It's quite chilling at times. Some enemies move incredibly fast and the audio queues for them can be nerve wracking when exploring certain areas. The ambiance adds to that experience as well as some great art direction and enemy design.

This is one of the most refreshing gaming experiences I've had in recent memories. If you want a solid action campaign with enthralling combat, climactic boss fights and likeable characters, I can't think of a title more deserving of that recommendation.

[h1]Plot[/h1]
After the incident of Raccoon City, The United States of America had no other choice but to stop the virus spread at any cost several attempts were made by local and federal agency none had success to contain the virus.

Having no choice left, the solution moved towards bombing, with both served as a means of destroying the mutants as well as serving to destroy any evidence in the city of Umbrella's bio-weapons project, which could be used by rival nations like China as a jumping-off point for their projects. Additionally, the destruction of this data would serve to wipe away evidence implying the US military was both aware and supportive of illegal bio-weapons development.

After seven days since the virus had spread throughout Raccoon City, the city was totally in chaos. Initially having a population with over 100.00 people, few managed to survive the initial days, even fewer managed to escape the city. 

On October 1st 1998, the United States government declared that Raccoon City was beyond saving and a missile strike was ordered so that the T-virus would not be allowed to spread any further. At dawn, two non-nuclear thermobaric missiles struck the city and wiped it off the face of the Earth. The events of the Raccoon City incident, including its destruction, were covered up by the Government.

A team was set up near the perimeter fence, took on responsibilities in destroying biohazardous material and killing or detaining current and former Umbrella employees suspected of smuggling bio-weaponry across the world, along with their customers. Immediately following the 1998 Raccoon City Destruction Incident, Anti-Umbrella Pursuit and Investigation Team was founded as a subordinate to USSTRATCOM. 

Leon Scott Kennedy, one of the few who witnesses the incident from inside and managed to escape that nightmare was brought in to interrogation by the US military, but the government was interested in recruiting him since he now possessed the experience they were looking. His subsequent training as a government agent turned him from a police rookie into an expert special agent, proficient in weapons handling and close-quarters combat.

Six years later, President's daughter was abducted on the way home from the University, in what had hallmarks of an inside job. American spies reported having seen the girl, Ashley Graham, in Spain and tracked her to an isolated, rural community. With all government agents being thoroughly investigated to identify the mole, Leon Kennedy was the one who had the least suspicion since he was well-known within the government for his feats, the agency chose him to search for the girl, suspecting any other agent may have ties with the kidnapping.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Resident Evil 4 did not follow the steps of Its predecessors; (RE 0, RE, RE 2 and RE 3) all of these game had a similar approach: survival horror. Resident Evil 4 is not a horror game like the early games of the franchise rather than a fully-fledged action game, this was the ditching point of its roots to becoming an action series.

Resident Evil 4 was the first title in the series to implement a third-person view rather than the original fixed camera angles its predecessors had. Its mechanics have been completely revamped to incorporate fast-paced gunplay, quick controls and shoot-outs involving massive crowds of enemies in more open areas. 

The camera in RE 4 is really bad, the movements are ok, but the camera doesnt follow the character's lead especially when you need to turn around while running or doing a 360 degree. Capcom again could've done a much better job with the PC version.

The saving system was also changed there are no ink ribbons anymore however, typewriters are still present. The game can be saved an infinite amount of times though there is a limit on how many different slots the player can save on. There is no chapter select either.

RE 4 implemented quick-time events, even during cutscenes, to keep the player more engaged. In a few instances, a QTE can appear during specific battles in real-time.  

Throughout most chapters in the game, Leon will be escorting Ashley through the map, the player can interact with Ashley, either "wait", "follow" or "hide". RE 4 is very similar to RE 0, where the game has two characters at the screen. Ashley does not fight, unlike Rebbeca or Billy and alike them If Ashley dies the mission is over. HELP, LEON!!! (Still got a headache even now)

The inventory is also remarkably different from any Resident Evil title, a case of which you'd expect an expert special agent to have. The new inventory now has a grid-like system where weapons and items have specific sizes which can be turned around in a "Tetris-like" fashion to fit into the case, this case, in my opinion, was the best of the series, kind of OP but allows the player to feel comfortable enough to get any item without worrying If X item is worth storing. The Storage Box was removed in RE 4.

Unlike the previous game where you had to grab a weapon from the scenario, in RE 4 you can buy them! The Merchant is another mechanic unique to Resident Evil 4, it's meant to be a "shop", but as a character. The Merchant has pre-determined spawns at various points of the game and will not harm the player.

[h1]Difficulty[/h1]
If I were to put RE 4 in my list of difficulty games of the franchise, It would be the easiest. The game rarely frightens the player, more like soften the experience with much more humanized enemies, Leon's sarcasm by making the whole game less scary or having a literal arsenal to choose from. I wanted to point one enemy who scares the creep out of me: Regenerators. That thing is terrifying.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Resident Evil 4 Ultimate HD Edition is a total joke. This game was released in 2005, fifteen years ago and Capcom did few adjustments compared to the original version, some HD textures here and there but nothing too significant whom two people did more than an entire team of devs, with limited access to data.

Thanks to @crismorales and @albert, these two incredible people created the RE4 HD Project, with the object of making an across-the-board HD revision of the textures, 3D models, lights effects and other aspects of the game, while respecting the look, tone, and intent of the originals. 

The work of these guys are beyond anything I've ever seen in the community, such a passion for a game deserves more than a simple mention from the devs, they practically Remaster the whole game from the Village to the Island! Before where you could only see blurring Paintings, they went after the original and put it into the game (They literally went after it, in SPAIN!) If before the atmosphere of this game was surreal it got even better thanks to their work.

I only bought the RE 4 Ultimate HD because of their work, I wanted to see if I could experience that same sensation when I first play the game, and I did! The scenario is by far the best of the franchise, with the HD Project, it reaches another level! 

[h1]Extra Mode[/h1]
All extra game modes are unlocked by completing the game once. They are;
Separate Ways - A large 5 chapter canon scenario that shows Ada's actions during the main game. The player can save during the game and visit the Merchant. It isn't present in the Gamecube version.

Assignment: Ada - A short non-canon scenario where the player controls Ada and must collect plaga samples. She has her own starting equipment and it takes place on the beginning parts of the island.

The Mercenaries - An arcade-style minigame with 4 maps, where the player can play with Leon, Ada, Krauser, Hawk and Wesker to kill enemies within a time limit and aim for a high score.

[h1]Overall[/h1]
Resident Evil 4 is a good game, but I only recommend it along with the @RE4 HD Project, if it was in any other platform I wouldn't suggest it to anyone!
